Notice Regarding California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determinations
Pursuant to CEQA, a "project" is defined as a "whole action" subject to a public agency's discretionary funding or approval that has the potential to either (1) cause a direct physical change in the environment or (2) cause a reasonably foreseeable indirect physical change in the environment. "Projects" include discretionary activity by a public agency, a private activity that receives any public funding, or activities that involve the public agency's issuance of a discretionary approval and is not statutorily or categorically exempt from CEQA. (Pub. Res. Code § 21065.) To the extent that matters listed in this Agenda are considered “projects” under CEQA, their appropriate CEQA determination will be listed below each recommendation. If no CEQA determination is listed, it has been determined that the action does not constitute a “project” under CEQA.
Viewing City Council Meetings
Members of the public may view the City Council meeting live on the City’s website https://www.azusaca.gov/1389/Watch-Meetings-Online, or on Channel 3 (Spectrum). Archived video of recorded meetings is also available on the City website. Your attendance at this public meeting may result in the recording and broadcast of your image and/or voice as previously described.
Procedures for Addressing the Council
The Council encourages interested people to address this legislative body by making public comments. Public comments may be made during designated agendized public comment periods and during public hearing items. Public comments are limited to five (5) minutes per speaker, unless a different time is announced by the Mayor/presiding Chair.
The Council encourages free expression of all points of view. To allow all persons the opportunity to speak, please keep your remarks brief. If others have already expressed your position, you may simply indicate that you agree with a previous speaker. If appropriate, a spokesperson may present the views of your entire group. State law generally prohibits the City Council from responding to or acting upon matters not listed on this agenda. Council rules prohibit clapping, booing, or shouts of approval or disagreement from the audience. Clapping, booing, shouting or other actions from the audience which, disturbs, impedes, or otherwise renders infeasible the meeting’s orderly conduct, who, after a request by the presiding officer, refuses to cease such behavior may be removed from the City Council chambers or remote participation platform.

When called, each person may address any item on or off the agenda during the public participation.

minutes_text:
CITY OF AZUSA
  MINUTES OF THE CITY COUNCIL, THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY
  TO THE FORMER REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY,
  THE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY
  REGULAR MEETING
  MONDAY, OCTOBER 3, 2022 – 7:30 P.M.

The City Council of the City of Azusa met in regular session at the above date and time in the Azusa Auditorium located
at 213 E. Foothill Boulevard, Azusa, CA 91702.

CLOSED SESSION

None.

REGULAR SESSION

Mayor Gonzales called the meeting to order at 7:30 P.M.

CITY COUNCIL ROLL CALL: Roll call was taken by City Clerk Cornejo.

PRESENT: COUNCILMEMBERS: ALVAREZ, AVILA Jr., BECKWITH, GONZALES, MENDEZ
ABSENT: COUNCILMEMBERS: NONE

The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Joe Guerra

Invocation was delivered by Rick Clark from Rising Church, in Azusa.

ALSO PRESENT

Elected Officials: City Clerk Cornejo.

Staff Members: City Manager Gonzalez, City Attorney Martinez, Chief of Police Wenrick, Deputy City Manager De
Anda-Scaia, Chief Deputy City Clerk Garcia and Deputy City Clerk II Hernandez.

CEREMONIAL

  1. Mayor Gonzales introduced Joe Guerra, the Chair of the Golden Days committee, to give a few
  presentations. Mr. Guerra presented the Council with bags in celebration of Golden Days.
  Councilmember Alvarez presented certificates for the Honored Citizens.
  2. City Manager Gonzalez and Public Works Director Delgadillo recognized three Public Works staff
  members, Jayson Tello, Vidal Villagomez Sr., and Joseph Alvarenga-Rodriguez, and shared their heroic
  efforts to help a motorist in need on the morning of September 17, 2022.

PUBLIC COMMENT

Rae Kearney and Mayra Rico, from Azusa Rotary, thanked the City of Azusa for co-sponsoring the Field of Glory Event
and they presented the City with a Freedom Flag. They also presented the Community Resources Department with a
donation.

Samira Mejia, a manager from Think Together, shared the importance of afterschool programs. She shared that the Think
Together organization will be having a Lights On Afterschool celebration on Wednesday, October 19th at Paramount
Elementary School.

REPORTS, UPDATES AND ANNOUNCEMENTS FROM STAFF/COUNCIL

City Manager Communications

City Manager Gonzalez shared that the Golden Days parade will take place on Saturday, October 8, 2022. He reported
that on October 13, 2022, the City Council will be meeting with the school board on the campus of Slauson Middle
School move the historic schoolhouse.
 Council Comments

Mayor Pro-Tem Mendez thanked the Azusa Golden Days Committee for their efforts and hard work in putting this event
together. He congratulated the three honored citizens who received their awards. He also thanked the Azusa Women’s
Club and Azusa Connects for the fun events they held.

Councilmember Alvarez reported that he attended the Chalktoberfest event and commended the artists for their talent. He
thanked all staff involved in putting these events together.

Councilmember Avila shared enthusiasm for Golden Days. He reported that the chalk fest was an amazing. He thanked
City Clerk Cornejo for encouraging everyone to get into the Golden Days spirit.

Councilmember Beckwith congratulated Azusa Pacific University for the inauguration of their 18th president. He reported
that he attended the Azusa Women’s Club event and the chalk fest and thanked them for the great kickoff.

Mayor Gonzales congratulations to the organizations for their very successful Golden Days events. He also thanked City
staff for making this event a success for the community.

SCHEDULED ITEMS – CITY COUNCIL

1. ADOPT RESOLUTION APPROVING THE THIRD AMENDMENT TO THE CITY MANAGER
EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT.

City Attorney Martinez provided a staff report.

Motion to approve Item D-1, 1) Adopt Resolution No. 2022-C76 of the City Council of the City of Azusa, California,
approving a Third Amendment to the City Manager Employment Agreement (Sergio Gonzalez), was made by
Councilmember Avila, seconded by Councilmember Beckwith, and carried by the unanimous vote of Council.

AYES:  COUNCILMEMBERS: ALVAREZ, AVILA Jr., BECKWITH, GONZALES, MENDEZ
NOES:  AGENCY MEMBERS: NONE
ABSTAIN:  AGENCY MEMBERS: NONE
ABSENT:  AGENCY MEMBERS: NONE

2. FIRST READING OF AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF AZUSA, CALIFORNIA, ADDING ARTICLE XI
TO CHAPTER 46 OFFENSES AND MISCELLANEOUS PROVISIONS TO THE AZUSA MUNICIPAL CODE
REGULATING CITY FACILITIES AND SUBJECTING THEM TO NIGHT TIME CLOSURE.

Deputy City Manager De Anda-Scaia provided a staff report.

Motion to approve Item D-2 was made by Councilmember Alvarez, seconded by Councilmember Mayor Pro-Tem
Mendez, and carried by the unanimous vote of Council.

AYES:  COUNCILMEMBERS: ALVAREZ, AVILA Jr., BECKWITH, GONZALES, MENDEZ
NOES:  AGENCY MEMBERS: NONE
ABSTAIN:  AGENCY MEMBERS: NONE
ABSENT:  AGENCY MEMBERS: NONE

CONSENT CALENDAR

1. The minutes of the Regular Meetings of July 18, 2022 and August 15, 2022 were approved as written.

2. Resolution No. 2022-C75 allowing certain claims and demands and specifying the funds out of which the same are to
  be paid was adopted.

3. The following Personnel Action Requests in accordance with the City of Azusa Civil Service Rules and applicable
  Memorandum of Understanding(s) were approved.

4. The purchase and upgrade of Fire Alarm Panel and Smoke/Duct Detectors (Life And Safety) equipment from Johnson
  Controls Fire Protection 12728 Shoemaker Ave. Santa Fe Springs, CA 90670 in the amount not to exceed
  $128,000.00; and Waive the competitive bidding process as authorized under Azusa Municipal Code Section 2-
  502(b) which provides exceptions for sole source providers were approved.

5. Waive the competitive bidding process as authorized under Azusa Municipal Code Section 2-502(b) which provides
  exceptions for sole source providers; and approval for the purchase of 15 tactical vests from TYR Tactical for the
  amount of $71,998.00 were approved.

6. Waive purchasing procedures as authorized under Azusa Municipal Code Section 2.539 and approval for the purchase
  of a CAT 420 backhoe loader and attachments in the amount not to exceed $186,725.14 from QUINN Company; and
   Authorization for the City Manager to execute a purchase agreement with QUINN Company for the purchase of the
  CAT 420 Backhoe Loader and proposed attachments were approved.

7. Authorization for Staff to solicit Bids to provide for the City Hall Restroom Remodel was approved.

8. Accept a grant award in the amount of $50,000 from Canyon City Foundation to the Community Resources
  Department; and Approval for necessary budget amendment and adjust the current fiscal year budget accordingly was
  approved.

9. Award the city-wide Classification and Compensation Study contract to Transformance Consulting in an amount not-
  to-exceed $146,200; and Authorization for the City Manager to execute the Professional Services Agreement between
  the City of Azusa and Transformance Consulting in a form acceptable to the City Attorney were approved.

Motion to approve Consent Calendar Items E-1 to E-9, was made by Mayor Pro-Tem Mendez, seconded by
Councilmember Avila, and carried by the unanimous vote of Council.

AYES:  COUNCILMEMBERS: ALVAREZ, AVILA Jr., BECKWITH, GONZALES, MENDEZ
NOES:  COUNCILMEMBERS: NONE
ABSTAIN:  COUNCILMEMBERS: NONE
ABSENT:  COUNCILMEMBERS: NONE

ADJOURNMENT

It was the consensus of the Council to adjourn the meeting in memory of Carmen Garcia, a life-long Azusa resident,
Arturo Uro, a life-long Azusa resident and San Juana Velazquez, a long-time Azusa resident. We adjourn in solemn honor
of Azusans who lost their lives to Covid-19.

TIME OF ADJOURNMENT: 8:20 P.M.

* Items heard out of order

CITY CLERK
